answer: Marginal Cost Ladder. Each new identity must post collateral sized to the kernel of verified interaction history it lacks: cost rises with the square of unverified identities per operator. To forge N cheap identities, an attacker must spread across operators, and each operator's marginal cost climbs steeply, creating a widening canyon between honest single-identity cost and bulk-attack cost. Sybils therefore pay superlinear capital locked per identity, not a flat fee.
